correctness.rationale: For all real beta>-1 and integer k>=0, Jacobi normalization gives the displayed probability cumulative energies. The parameter-contiguous relation q=p-(1-t)r and shifted Jacobi ODE imply a first-order two-polynomial system and a differentiated boundary identity. The boundary term vanishes at zero, proving the exact integral factorization. For k>=1, q^2-(1-t)r^2 has degree 2k, is strictly negative at the k zeros of p and strictly positive at the k-1 interlaced zeros of p derivative and at both endpoints; hence exactly 2k distinct simple interior zeros and sign reversals. The k=0 case is explicit. The embedded checker replays 191 supplementary algebraic/endpoint/root-bracketing assertions across 35 finite parameter-degree pairs. Its finite scope is not offered as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Comparison is at the level of the exact cumulative squared-energy difference and the implication of 2k transverse crossings. The closest Zernike source contains definitions/orthogonality/recurrence but not this classification in the inspected relevant main and appendix material. The classical Jacobi interlacing source concerns roots of Jacobi polynomials, not cumulative energy differences. A mathematically distinct Zernike comparison compares (k,beta) to (k-1,beta+2) at fixed total degree and gives nonnegative tangencies; it neither covers nor implies the fixed-k, beta-to-beta+1 order reversals. Searches of published-finding corpus and the external literature did not return an equivalent or dominating statement. This is best-knowledge novelty, not independently certified global priority.
residual_risks: An unindexed classical Jacobi parameter-contiguous integral identity may already imply or explicitly state this all-degree crossing count; no proof of bibliographic uniqueness is claimed.
The assertion is specific to normalized single-mode energies. Reinterpretation as joint multimode compression eigenvalues would be invalid; such claims are expressly excluded.

value.rationale: The normalized centered-disk energy is a natural invariant of each orthogonal Zernike optical/ball mode, and k counts its interior radial nodes. Identifying the exact number 2k of sign-reversing concentration-order swaps for each adjacent angular pair, all dimensions and the full continuous Jacobi weight range is a complete structural classification, with location brackets at every mode node and turning point. It qualitatively separates a fixed-radial-index angular step from the previously established fixed-total-degree shift, where all contacts are tangential. This motivated universal crossing fact is not just a recomputed table or a minor numerical improvement.
